verdicts.where: Path of Exile's Arctic Armour (less harm from hits while stationary) and its 'while moving' defences; BattleTech's Brace against evasion earned by moving; hiding behind pillars from raid-boss blasts in World of Warcraft. No game found that maps three kinds of harm to three foot postures for both sides.

Warhammer 40,000: Darktide's toughness, health and corruption (one layer regenerates, one does not, one is healed only at a station); trauma in Back 4 Blood; Halo shields; one-hit block charges. Setting the layer by how long the attack was shown is in none of them.

The ghost train in Pac-Man Championship Edition DX (enemies fall in behind you and the train's length is the prize); 'training' monsters in EverQuest. A follower status that makes the enemy faster, riper and countable is its own.

Critical distance for bows and bowguns in Monster Hunter (a range band where harm is best); the tipper sweet spot in Smash Bros; Close and Distant enemy states in Diablo 4. None asks for the band to be held over time or pays in earlier warnings.

The tow cable in Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (circle the walker several times to bind it); capture loops in Pokemon Ranger; combo points built and spent on one target. Winding one way and unwinding the other is not in them.

Zombie Highway (zombies leap onto your car, each one weighs it down, none lets go, and you scrape them off by sideswiping roadside wrecks at speed); the same in Mad Max and State of Decay; Micro-Goombas that cling to Mario and slow him.
verdicts.mutation: Let clingers be passed on, not scraped off: brushing within 0.8 m of a warden, keeper or other large enemy at speed moves every clinger onto it, where they drag and bite it instead. Stone does nothing; the cure is a dangerous neighbour.

verdicts.where: Warlock's Fatal Bonds in Dota 2 (linked enemies each take a share of harm dealt to any one of them) and Domino in Dishonored 2. The trigger, crossing your own wake, is new, but the condition it applies is that link plus a slow.
verdicts.mutation: Make the knot a rope, not a harm-share: knotted enemies are tied to the crossing point in the order they followed and can move only round it at rope's length; shoving or felling one jerks the next into it.

verdicts.where: Clickers in The Last of Us and Eyeless Dogs in Lethal Company (blind hunters that lose you when you stand still and go to the last noise); thrown-bottle lures; Brogue halving stealth range while you do not move.
verdicts.mutation: Do not make the player vanish. Let every sigil impact linger as a fading sound for a few seconds, and let a still player's crowd divide among those sounds by loudness, so where the last casts landed decides how the crowd splits.

verdicts.where: Approaches in Fate Accelerated and action ratings in Blades in the Dark (stats that are ways of acting, not kinds of person); attribute requirements on gear in Diablo 2 and Path of Exile, with their 'while stationary' and 'while moving' tags. Stats named for stop, go, near and wait are its own.

Light-cycle walls in Tron; Blaze in Diablo 2 and Singed's poison trail in League of Legends (harm laid by walking); laser fences between posts in Command & Conquer. A line whose strength is the length of an unbroken straight walk is not in them.

The Spy with the Cloak and Dagger in Team Fortress 2 (stand still unseen while enemies walk past, then stab their backs); the stealth-then-backstab opener of rogues in World of Warcraft; Brotato's Soldier, who attacks only while still.
verdicts.mutation: Drop the bonus on backs. Let Last Word run down the file of enemies in the order they walked past the Mute, each stroke stronger than the one before, so the Mute wants a long single-file stream and not merely turned backs.

verdicts.where: Timed light-every-torch puzzles in Zelda; totem upkeep classes and EverQuest bards twisting short songs; perk machines at fixed places in Call of Duty Zombies. A class that is a round of fixed posts kept against the wave clock is its own.
Mars's Bulwark in Dota 2 (a passive shield that cuts harm arriving in the front arc by facing alone, with no button) and Bristleback's armoured rear; the shield-bash tank class generally.
verdicts.mutation: Give the plank weight: it keeps the heading of one second ago and swings round after the turn, so a quick turn leaves the new front bare and the old side covered, and every corner is planned around where the bier still points.

verdicts.where: The original Aurelion Sol in League of Legends (stars orbit at a fixed radius, hit only at that radius, and enemies inside the orbit are untouched); King Bible and Unholy Vespers in Vampire Survivors; Darius's outer-ring blade.
verdicts.mutation: Pay for the empty middle, not the orbit: each swing's harm is multiplied by the enemies in the band and divided by those inside it, so a clean interior is the weapon and one enemy let inside spoils the stroke.

verdicts.where: Pac-Man Championship Edition DX: lead an ever longer train of ghosts, grow greedy, then turn back and run down the whole train for a prize that rises with its length. Only the trigger differs, a U-turn in place of a pellet.
verdicts.mutation: Do not harm the train: turn it. The wave about-faces each enemy In Procession and marches it back down the wake for 3 s, trampling whatever comes behind; harm is done by the turned bodies and counted by how many were turned.

verdicts.where: Brotato's Lucky character and Baby Elephant item (picking up a material deals harm to a random enemy); Money = Power in The Binding of Isaac (harm per coin held).
verdicts.mutation: Let each pickup fire from where it lay back along the straight line to the previous pickup, piercing everything on that segment, so the order in which the shards are gathered draws the attack.

verdicts.where: Capture loops in Pokemon Ranger; winding up Bowser by rotating the stick in Super Mario 64; Zangief's full-circle motion; spinning one way or the other to choose Alcremie's form in Pokemon Sword and Shield. A walked circle stored one way and released the other is its own.
Qix and Libble Rabble (close a shape to claim what is inside); Disruptor's Kinetic Field in Dota 2 (a ring enemies cannot leave). A pen made of three walked straight lines is not in them.
Sneak-attack rules in Skyrim and Dishonored (an unaware enemy takes a multiplied hit and dies without alerting the rest); hiding-spot kills in Assassin's Creed as guards pass within reach.
verdicts.mutation: Let Passed change where they go, not how hard they are hit: a Passed enemy has paid its respects and will not turn back for 5 s whatever the Mute then does, so standing in the stream sorts the crowd into gone and still coming.

verdicts.where: Templar Assassin's Psionic Trap in Dota 2 (stronger the longer it has sat before you set it off); a paladin's Seal spent by Judgement in World of Warcraft. Snuffing a fixed post you were keeping lit, for its age, is its own.

The Meat Wagon in Warcraft 3 (gathers up to eight corpses to carry); Bone Wall in Diablo 2; deployable cover in Gears of War. A wall paid for in kills made while advancing and set down by stopping is its own.

Io's Spirits In and Out in Dota 2 and Aurelion Sol's expanding stars (an orbit whose radius the player changes); zeroing a scope to a ranged target in Arma. Setting the radius by letting an enemy come close and then stopping is not in them.

SUPERHOT (the world moves only when you move); Goriyas in Zelda: A Link to the Past, which move only when Link moves. Halting only those who were led, to switch them from runner to stander, is its own.
The Throw command in Final Fantasy (hurl a weapon from the pack for harm set by its quality; it is used up) and Fling in Pokemon; Tediore reload-throws in Borderlands 2; the Coin Gun in Terraria.
verdicts.mutation: Throw the history, not the object: the thrown item bursts once per notch and is left lying blank where it fell, to be picked up and notched again, so what is spent is the tolls it was carried through.

verdicts.where: The Inverted Song of Time and Song of Double Time in Majora's Mask (the player slows or hastens the doom clock); Chronostasis in Lightning Returns; walking a capstan round in Sea of Thieves. Winding the wave clock by walked circles is its own.

Turrets dropped at the player's feet on a timer in Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor; Brands in Path of Exile; the ramping Inferno Tower in Clash of Clans. A mark that is simply the last deliberate stop is not in them.
Pokemon Ranger (a loop is made when the line crosses itself, and pays on what is inside); loop closing in Paper.io. Paying at the crossing point itself, for the train caught there, was not found.

Whip and Knife in Vampire Survivors (fire along the facing, front and back); tail guns in Gradius; the Lance charge in Monster Hunter that builds while running straight. A rear shot that meters seconds without turning is its own.

Pacifism gates in Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 (fly between two posts to set off a blast); graze in Touhou and near-miss boost in Burnout. A gap made by two enemies, who then give the shot its line, was not found.

Archero (stand still to attack, move to stop); Shadow Pinion in Vampire Survivors (builds while moving, fires on stopping); pull-and-release aiming in Monster Strike. Stillness as the charge and the first step as the aim is its own.

Periodic pulses in Vampire Survivors (Pentagram, La Borra); the fourth-beat finisher in Hi-Fi Rush; effects that fire on the day tick in Loop Hero. A weapon that keeps the quarters of the wave clock is its own.

Skills that grow with the count of enemies near (Legion Commander's Overwhelming Odds in Dota 2; harm per nearby enemy in Path of Exile). Distant: nothing found that weighs the crowd on one hand against the crowd on the other and strikes the lighter side.

Hoodwink's Bushwhack and Windranger's Shackleshot in Dota 2 (skills that work only with a tree in reach); Geomancy in Final Fantasy Tactics; fighting from cover in Gears of War. An attack that starts at the obstacle and favours its far side is its own.
Searing Bond in Path of Exile: a planted totem joined to the player by a burning beam that harms whatever touches it, swept by walking. Io's Tether in Dota 2 is the same line between two bodies.
verdicts.mutation: Make the rope rake, not burn: enemies it meets are carried along its sweep, and when it goes slack each one takes harm for every metre it was dragged, so the arc walked gathers a heap and then pays for it.

verdicts.where: Tower markers in Final Fantasy XIV raids (be inside the ring when it resolves or the result is worse); a mage's Rune of Power in World of Warcraft; delayed air-strike markers. A self-set rendezvous that upgrades the player's own strike is its own.

Drag-select rectangles in strategy games; area claimed by closed lines in Qix; Concentrated Effect in Path of Exile (less area, more harm). All distant: nothing found that strikes the bounding box of where the feet have been.

Shadow Pinion in Vampire Survivors (builds while you move, strikes when you stop) and Archero, whose whole control is lift the thumb to attack. The claim that no game treats the lifted thumb as a trigger is wrong.
verdicts.mutation: Make it a brake-check: the stamp waits 0.6 s after the stop and its harm is multiplied by the followers that run into the player's back in that time, so the train piling up, not the length of the run, is the stroke.

verdicts.where: Unleash Support in Path of Exile (stores up to three repeats of the spell and lets them all go at once), with Archero's stop-to-fire as the release.
verdicts.mutation: Keep the stop as the trigger but let the walk place the targets: each stored cast is tied to one sharp corner turned since the last release and lands on that corner, so the path sets the marks and the stop only fires them.

verdicts.where: Options in Gradius: helpers that sit exactly where the ship was a moment ago along its path and fire its weapons from there. Ekko's trailing afterimage in League of Legends marks the same past position.
verdicts.mutation: Make it a rear-guard that is dropped and held: the figure stays at the spot 2 s back until no enemy is left within 3 m of it, and only then jumps to the new spot, so it finishes a clump before it follows.

verdicts.where: 'While moving' and 'while stationary' conditions on supports and gear in Path of Exile; Hermes' boons in Hades that pay for speed; momentum upgrades in survivor games. A bonus for not turning, with a silence charged for each corner, is its own.

Spell Echo and spell totems in Path of Exile (a repeat, or a cast from another origin); Qiyana in League of Legends drawing power from the nearest wall. A repeat that comes from the nearest piece of the map is its own.
Gil Toss in Final Fantasy (spend money for harm); the Microtransaction Gun in Enter the Gungeon and the Coin Gun in Terraria (currency as ammunition); Money = Power in The Binding of Isaac.
verdicts.mutation: Pawn it, do not burn it: each cast leaves one carried coin lying where the cast landed for 10 s; walking back over it redeems it, and unredeemed coins sink. The price of the bonus is a journey into where you just struck.

verdicts.where: Buzz in Psyvariar and the Tension system in Shikigami no Shiro (near misses charge the weapon); graze in Touhou. Standing at the edge of a shown strike is the same near miss without a dodge.
verdicts.mutation: Let the near miss lend its shape, not a free cast: the sigil's next cast takes the outline and size of the strike that just missed (ring, wedge or line), so the player chooses which enemy attack to stand beside in order to borrow it.

verdicts.where: Unleash Support in Path of Exile (stored casts let go together); pooling everything for the two-minute burst window in Final Fantasy XIV raids. Release on a public wave clock the player cannot hurry is its own.

Mana reserved by auras in Path of Exile; opt-in burdens such as the Demon Bell in Sekiro and the Pact of Punishment in Hades; the holdout ring in Risk of Rain 2. A reserved pool that is warning time, held by breakable promises, is its own.

The Vow of Poverty feat in Dungeons & Dragons 3.5 (Book of Exalted Deeds): own almost nothing and receive standing bonuses, under the same name. Also Hollow Palm Technique in Path of Exile and conducts in NetHack.
verdicts.mutation: Pay for refusals made within reach: the vow counts each item the character comes within 2 m of and leaves lying until it sinks, and the bonus grows with that count, so poverty is earned by walking past things, not by a cap.

verdicts.where: Rolling upkeep buffs that fall off if not refreshed in time (Lifebloom stacks in World of Warcraft); lap streaks in racing games; passing the campfire each loop in Loop Hero. A stack kept by one visit to a place per wave period is its own.

Bloodstains in Dark Souls (your currency waits where you were); the money tree in Animal Crossing (bury coin, come back for more); the well-done window on the spit in Monster Hunter. A small bell-timed heap that doubles in a 6 s window is its own.

Wave flags in Kingdom Rush (they show where the next wave enters and pay a bonus for acting on them); emergence tiles in Into the Breach; shrines charged by standing in a ring. One ring that is both forecast and offer is its own.
Active reload in Gears of War; the Aim Ring in Lost Odyssey (a closing ring and a timed release); the rocket start in Mario Kart. A timing window measured as the length of a stillness is its own.

Curse in Vampire Survivors (faster enemies for more reward); the Shrine of the Mountain in Risk of Rain 2; each loop not retreated from in Loop Hero. Stacks earned by refusing an open exit, and shown on the next one, are its own.
The Warbanner in Risk of Rain and Risk of Rain 2: on every level-up a banner is planted where the player stands and strengthens anyone inside its ring for the rest of the stage.
verdicts.mutation: Mark what was refused, not where the level came: the chimes not taken leave rings on the ground that hold a weak form of what they offered while stood in, so the map of shelters is made of the choices turned down.

verdicts.where: Sprint in every shooter (faster, weapon lowered), on the push-the-stick-further control of PUBG Mobile and Call of Duty Mobile; walk and run by stick tilt since Super Mario 64. A new name on the stock sprint.

Dashes with invulnerable frames in Hades; Phasing in Path of Exile (pass through enemies); the quick turn in Resident Evil. A pass-through earned by the U-turn itself, which also turns the crowd, was not found.

The ghost train in Pac-Man Championship Edition DX (enemies follow the path behind you in a line); Cosmic Clones in Super Mario Galaxy 2 and Badeline in Celeste; monsters following scent in Brogue. As the steering rule of a whole horde it is its own.

Red light, green light as an enemy: Pyretic and Acceleration Bomb in Final Fantasy XIV (punished for moving inside a marked window), the doll in Squid Game adaptations, monsters that hunt by the sound of motion.
verdicts.mutation: Let it throw at the path, not the player: one shot per half second moved, each landing on the stretch of wake walked in that half second. Moving while it listens then lays a bombardment the player can draw through the train.

verdicts.where: Cosmic Clones in Super Mario Galaxy 2 and Badeline in Celeste (pursuers that run your exact path); tracker dogs in Metal Gear Solid 3. A trail-runner that is thrown off where the path crosses itself was not found.

Beamos statues in Zelda (an eye that sweeps one way, approached from behind its turn); slow-turning tank destroyers circled in World of Tanks; strafing to an enemy's shield side in Dark Souls. Left- and right-built variants shown in the shape are its own.

Laser barriers strung between emitter pairs in shoot-em-ups such as Gradius; gates in Geometry Wars; the marching wall swarms that cross the field in Vampire Survivors. One advancing line read as gaps and non-gaps is its own.

The donut attack of every raid and action boss (Dynamo-type attacks in Final Fantasy XIV, halberd sweeps in Dark Souls): a ring that hits at range and is safe at the feet. A long pole does not change the rule.

The alarm-runner: guards who run to ring the alarm bell in Assassin's Creed, orcs who run to sound the horn in Shadow of Mordor, the Screamer in 7 Days to Die; leakers in tower defence. Stop him or the next wave comes early.
verdicts.mutation: Make him the toll, not a threat to it: one ringer walks to the post every period and the bell rings when he arrives, early if his way is clear and late if crowd, stone or the player stand in it; killing him loses that toll's reward too.

verdicts.where: Elites leading Grunts in Halo (kill the leader and the crowd behaves differently); artillery spotters in Company of Heroes; the Screamer in 7 Days to Die. An enemy that only improves how the crowd is aimed is its own.

Hazards on one shared beat: Beat Blocks in Super Mario Galaxy 2, every enemy acting on the beat in Crypt of the NecroDancer and Hi-Fi Rush. Platform crushers are often synced across a level, so the shared phase is not new.
verdicts.mutation: Do not strike together: let the stroke travel outward from the bell-post at walking pace, each Jack striking as it reaches him, so the field shows a moving wave to walk with or cut through, and a killed Jack leaves a hole in it.

verdicts.where: Ambushes drawn to extraction points in The Division's Dark Zone; shopkeepers and guards waiting at the exit in Spelunky and Shiren the Wanderer; half-room sweeps in Final Fantasy XIV. A gate guard that exists only because of the load, and is as strong as it, is its own.

Paper.io and Slither.io (a rival closes a loop round you and what is inside dies); Qix; Moldorm in Zelda, hurt only at one end. A keeper built wholly on walking the bounds round the player is its own.

Enemy intents in Slay the Spire; turn-order bars in Grandia and Final Fantasy X; boss-timer bars in raid add-ons; Simon-says bosses. A public row that changes by one neighbour swap each pass, as bell-ringers change, was not found.

The Warpriest's aura in Destiny's King's Fall raid (stand in the bearer's ring or die); the closing circle of battle royales; darkness that kills outside the light in Don't Starve. A keeper who is the moving safe band, with a deadly middle, is its own.

The Inlaid Library and Gallo Tower in Vampire Survivors (corridor stages where the horde comes only from the two ends); mazes with doors that change in Lady Bug. A grid of such lanes whose joints the wave clock rearranges is its own.

Moving shade in V Rising (day and night are places, and the boundary moves with the sun); sweeping clock-hand hazards in clock-tower boss rooms; lighthouse beams. A district that is the wave clock drawn on the ground is its own.

The pipe bomb in Left 4 Dead and Decoy Totem in Path of Exile (the horde goes to the noise); pillar halls such as Anor Londo's in Dark Souls. A lure that is whichever pillar the automatic attacks strike is its own.

The Sphere Grid in Final Fantasy X and the Crystarium in Final Fantasy XIII (growth as travel along a board); the Stat Matrix in Kingdom Hearts Re:coded. One unbranching line, undone only from its head, that may cross itself, was not found.

The Lilium Orb in Tales of Xillia (activate the nodes round a cell and the skill inside is granted); Intuitive Leap and Thread of Hope in Path of Exile; Go and Dots and Boxes. A free-form fence drawn by the route is its own.

The mana curve in Hearthstone and Magic (a cost-N card comes into play from turn N); turn-numbered relics in Slay the Spire; neutral item tiers that unlock by game time in Dota 2. A tree whose rings switch on by wave count is its own.

Paragon glyphs in Diablo 4 and radius jewels in Path of Exile (a socket that counts what is allocated around it); adjacency bonuses in Backpack Battles and Luck be a Landlord. Counting only an unbroken straight line through the node is its own.

Familiarity in Nioh and the Evolver in Enter the Gungeon (an item that grows as it is used); veiled Riven mods in Warframe; found-in-raid status in Escape from Tarkov. Worth counted in waves carried through unbanked, with no tiers, is its own.

Hero weapons in Fable III (they change by how you played); weapon affinities in Vagrant Story (grown by what the weapon was used on); skills by use in The Elder Scrolls; 'while stationary' modifiers in Path of Exile. A line written by a posture and working only in it is its own.

Shiren the Wanderer (carry your best gear into the dungeon to improve it, lose it all on death); the one-property reroll at the Mystic in Diablo 3; destroy-on-failure enchanting in Lineage. A reroll steered by how you walk the next wave is its own.
The Orologion in Vampire Survivors (all enemies frozen); restraint rewarded by mercy in Undertale and by Pacifism in Geometry Wars. A free freeze that pays more for not using it is its own.

Blending with a walking group of scholars in Assassin's Creed (keep their slow pace inside the group); tiptoeing by half tilt in Super Mario 64; tailing missions. A procession that is also a wall to the horde is its own.

Timed doors in Dead Cells and the Boss Rush door in The Binding of Isaac; paid or conditional extracts in Escape from Tarkov; the top of the flagpole in Super Mario Bros. Two exits open at once, the better one through the crowd, is its own.
Pacifism mode in Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2: lead a train of pursuers through a gate and the gate destroys what follows you, the bigger the train the better. The arch is that gate.
verdicts.mutation: Make it count, not kill: those passing under are bowed and held in the order they come, forming a file; when the arch falls one blow runs down the file and grows with each body. A mob arriving abreast jams it.

verdicts.where: Untouchable-but-harmless states: Ghost Scepter in Dota 2, Wraith's phase in Apex Legends, Ice Block in World of Warcraft, Zhonya's Hourglass in League of Legends; granted here by a stand-on-it shrine as in Diablo.
verdicts.mutation: Make sanctuary a place held, not a state carried: safety lasts only within arm's reach of the knocker, the dead mass at the edge and wait, and every unused second of the 37 is paid out, so the question is when to let go and walk out.

verdicts.where: God Mode in Hades (each death adds lasting resistance); Reventure (each new way to die is a reward); the Morgue in Don't Starve and morgue files in Dungeon Crawl. A death that lengthens the warning of the very attack that caused it is its own.

Legacy heroes in Wildermyth; relics of dead heroes in Massive Chalice; constellations made from how a hero was played in Moon Hunters; the graveyard and fame bonuses in Realm of the Mad God. A permanent tree whose nodes are your own dead is its own.

Lunar Coins in Risk of Rain 2 (saved the moment they are picked up, kept through death or quitting); Darkness in Hades; survival-time milestone rewards in Survivor.io. A meta-currency safe at once and paid by time survived is standard.
verdicts.mutation: Pay by where the toll was heard: the Nth toll pays N Echoes times the number of different landmarks of the district the character has stood beside at a toll this vigil, still credited at once, so each bell asks for a new place.

verdicts.where: Choose-one item pedestals in The Binding of Isaac and perk altars in Noita; the carousel in Teamfight Tactics (walk into your pick against a timer); perk machines reached mid-horde in Call of Duty Zombies. As the replacement for every level-up pause it is its own.

Extraction timers in Escape from Tarkov and Hunt: Showdown (stand in the exit zone while the count runs; leave it and the count resets); deposit time that grows with the amount carried in Deep Rock Galactic.
verdicts.mutation: Hand the load through piece by piece: one carried item is banked every half second in an order the player sets, the character goes last, and stepping out keeps what has already gone through, so a pressed player can bank part and run.

verdicts.where: Acceleration Bomb in Final Fantasy XIV (be motionless at the instant the countdown ends); musical statues; freeze-on-the-signal minigames in Mario Party. The rule is the same, with a reward in place of a penalty.
verdicts.mutation: Ask for a self-set rite, not stillness: whatever the body was doing at the first toll (standing, walking one heading, circling one way) must be done again at each later stroke to keep it, with the crowd arranged differently every time.

verdicts.where: Death's Door in Darkest Dungeon; Fight For Your Life in Borderlands; the escape pod in EVE Online (lose ship and cargo, keep the pilot); the Doom countdown in Final Fantasy. A reprieve whose length is whatever the wave clock has left is its own.

Throw Money in Assassin's Creed II (the crowd gathers on what you threw) and the Alluring Skull in Dark Souls; hold-to-charge releases; Unleash Support in Path of Exile. Two buttons that both cost the player's own loot or own attacks is its own.
Spore (each stage totals how you played and hands you the archetype and power that fit); Digimon evolving by how they were raised; the class suggested from tutorial behaviour in Oblivion.
verdicts.mutation: Let the classes come and watch: each guild figure stands in the district where its act is easiest and counts only what is done within its sight; the one that saw most steps forward, so a player can court a class by performing where its master can see.
